newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds steady, more crown losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds steady, more crown losses seen.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were flat in the early session on Friday, while the crown lost ground and was seen falling more because of worries about EMU.
The market was focussing the French election on Sunday and the Swedish ruling party's view on EMU which will be revealed on June 3 at 1430 GMT.

"Now we have seen some buying from London-based investment banks. The market is playing a waiting game with a nervous undertone. The level 4.56/4.57 against the mark should nevertheless hold," one dealer said.
"After the French election and the Social Democrats announcement on their EMU decision on Tuesday, the crown could well recover," the dealer added.
Six month T-bill rates were flat at 4.32 percent and the ten-year bond yields were unchanged at 7.11 percent.
The crown softened to 4.5430 against the mark from 4.5350 late on Thursday.
